_README: Model bake-off arms. Fill in every FILL_IN before running.
scripts/bakeoff.py refuses to start while any FILL_IN remains, so a
typo fails immediately instead of 20 resumes into a paid run.
model_id  : the exact API string. Not the marketing name. A wrong id
fails at request time and reads like a model problem.
base_url  : prefilled with each provider's documented OpenAI-compatible
endpoint. VERIFY THESE -- they move, and regional endpoints
differ (Zhipu in particular has a separate international host).
api_key_env: the env var to read. Nothing is read from .env automatically.
pricing   : USD per 1M tokens. Leave null and the run still works --
it reports tokens and latency, and omits dollars rather
extra_body: merged into the request as-is. Put reasoning effort here;
the key differs per provider ('reasoning_effort', etc).
send_temperature: false for models that reject temperature at any value.

arms.name: anthropic-control
arms.notes: The config in production today. The only arm whose numbers are already trusted.

arms.name: gpt-5.6-luna-medium
arms.notes: Published rates: $0.20 in / $0.02 cached in / $1.20 out per 1M. cache_write is 0 -- OpenAI does not bill for writing to the cache. token_param and send_temperature are set for a reasoning model.

arms.name: haiku-panel-bare
arms.notes: Reproduces PLAN.md section 8a on the 20-resume sample: Haiku panel, no JSON enforcement. Expected to fail ~49% of panel calls. Present as the control for haiku-panel-prefill -- without it, a good prefill result cannot be attributed to the prefill.

arms.name: haiku-panel-prefill
arms.notes: Same model, same prompt, with the assistant turn prefilled with '{' so the model cannot open with prose. Tests section 8a's own hypothesis that Haiku's 49% failure rate was a structured-output problem, not a capability problem.

arms.name: gemini-3.7-flash-medium
arms.notes: BLOCKED 2026-08-27: this key is on the Gemini free tier, capped at 20 requests per day per model. One 20-resume run needs 60+ (20 x 3 panel agents), so the arm cannot complete. Enable billing on the Google Cloud project to unblock; nothing in this config needs to change. model_id is CONFIRMED valid -- the quota error names the model, so it resolved. Rates: $0.75 in / $3.75 out per 1M, 90% cache discount. concurrency 2 because 5 resumes x 3 agents is 15 requests in flight.

arms.name: haiku-panel-unwrapped
arms.notes: Same bare Haiku panel as haiku-panel-bare, run AFTER _unwrap_panel_score landed. The pair isolates what the parser fix is worth: 60 of 78 failures in the bare run were valid JSON wrapped in a dimension-keyed envelope.

arms.name: anthropic-control-60
arms.notes: Full 60-resume corpus, for re-fitting the verdict cutoffs on more than 20 points and for a held-out cutoff test. Distinct arm name so the 20-resume results for anthropic-control are not overwritten.

arms.name: gpt-5.6-luna-60
arms.notes: Full 60-resume corpus, for re-fitting the verdict cutoffs on more than 20 points and for a held-out cutoff test. Distinct arm name so the 20-resume results for gpt-5.6-luna-medium are not overwritten.

arms.name: luna-single-pass
arms.notes: The control for the cascade itself: same model, same cached system block, same extraction step, same personas -- but all three dimensions scored in ONE call instead of three parallel ones plus a conditional arbiter. The cascade's entire justification is that it beats this. Never measured until now.

arms.name: luna-effort-low
arms.notes: Same model and prompts, reasoning_effort='low' instead of 'medium'. Output tokens are 69% of the bill and ~75% of them are reasoning, not visible rationale (271 chars ~= 68 tokens against ~290 output tokens per call), so effort is the lever and rationale length is not.

run._swap_slots_note: Which model slots the arm's model replaces. Extraction (triage) stays on Haiku in every arm so the comparison isolates scoring, and matches PLAN.md section 8a.
run._concurrency_note: Default for arms that do not set their own. An arm can override with a top-level "concurrency" field when its provider rate-limits.
